questions.stem: The Sangeet Natak Akademi officially recognises how many classical dance forms of India?

options.option_text: 8 (Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Sattriya)

questions.explanation: CLASSICAL DANCES OF INDIA — recognised by the SANGEET NATAK AKADEMI + the Ministry of Culture. The traditional count is 8 (OR 9 if you include Chhau which SNA added in 2010). MNEMONIC ('BK²M²OSK'): BHARATANATYAM (TN), KATHAK (UP/N. India), KATHAKALI (Kerala), KUCHIPUDI (AP), MANIPURI (Manipur), MOHINIYATTAM (Kerala), ODISSI (Odisha), SATTRIYA (Assam). KEY CRITERIA for 'classical': based on NATYASHASTRA (treatise by BHARATA MUNI, ~2nd c. BCE-2nd c. CE); follows structured Nritta (pure dance), Nritya (expressive), Natya (drama) elements; uses codified abhinaya (expression) — Angika (body), Vachika (speech), Aharya (costume), Sattvika (emotion). GLOBAL RECOGNITION: many classical dances are UNESCO ICH — Kutiyattam (2008), Ramlila, Chhau (2010). REGIONS → DANCES (match set): TAMIL NADU = Bharatanatyam; UP/RAJASTHAN/N. INDIA = Kathak; KERALA = Kathakali + Mohiniyattam; ANDHRA PRADESH = Kuchipudi; ODISHA = Odissi; MANIPUR = Manipuri; ASSAM = Sattriya; SERAIKELA/MAYURBHANJ/PURULIA (Jharkhand/Odisha/WB) = Chhau. Folk dances are separate + vast (Garba, Bhangra, Lavani, Bihu, Ghoomar, etc.). Very high-frequency SSC + Railway + State PSC topic. some sources also include Chhau making it 9.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: BHARATANATYAM, the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, was originally known as:
questions.explanation: BHARATANATYAM — the OLDEST of Indian classical dances (~2000 years old); originated in TEMPLES of Tamil Nadu. EARLIER NAMES: 'SADIR', 'Dasi Attam', 'Chinna Melam' — performed by DEVADASIS (temple dancers consecrated to deities). 1910s British colonial anti-nautch movement + Madras Presidency's 1947 Devadasi Abolition Act stigmatised + outlawed temple dancing. REVIVAL: Rukmini Devi Arundale (Theosophist + social reformer) + E. Krishna Iyer rescued the form, renamed it BHARATA NATYAM ('Bharat's dance' / combining BHA-va, RA-ga, TA-la). Rukmini founded KALAKSHETRA at Adyar (1936), where Bharatanatyam is rigorously taught to this day. ETYMOLOGY: (a) From Bharata Muni, author of Natya Shastra. (b) Folk etymology as above (bhava+raga+tala). TECHNIQUE: based on Natya Shastra + Abhinaya Darpana. Uses ARAMANDI (half-seated posture), MUDRAS (hand gestures — ~108 single-hand, 28 combined), aramandi, aduvus (basic movements), Nritta (pure)-Nritya (expressive)-Natya (dramatic). STANDARD REPERTOIRE (Margam, codified by the TANJORE QUARTET in 1800s): Alarippu → Jatiswaram → Shabdam → Varnam → Padam/Javali → Tillana. COSTUME: silk saree pleated + stitched; elaborate temple jewellery. MUSIC: Carnatic. LEADING EXPONENTS: Rukmini Devi, Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam, Sonal Mansingh, Alarmel Valli, Malavika Sarukkai. practised by DEVADASIS in Tamil temples; renamed Bharatanatyam in the 1930s by RUKMINI DEVI ARUNDALE.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

_fixes.was: SADIR / DASI ATTAM — practised by DEVADASIS in Tamil temples; renamed Bharatanatyam in the 1930s by RUKMINI DEVI ARUNDALE
_fixes.moved_to_explanation: practised by DEVADASIS in Tamil temples; renamed Bharatanatyam in the 1930s by RUKMINI DEVI ARUNDALE

questions.stem: KATHAK, the classical dance of North India, has three major GHARANAS (schools). Which of these is NOT a Kathak gharana?
questions.explanation: KATHAK — classical dance of North India (UP, Rajasthan, MP, Delhi). NAME: from Sanskrit 'katha' = story, and 'kathakars' = storytellers. EVOLVED from temple recitation (of Ramayana/Mahabharata) to Mughal courts (secularised + Persian-influenced). THREE MAJOR GHARANAS of KATHAK: (1) LUCKNOW gharana — emphasis on GRACE + ABHINAYA (expression); evolved in court of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah (himself a great patron); exponents = Bindadin Maharaj, Achhan Maharaj, Shambhu Maharaj, BIRJU MAHARAJ (1938-2022; most celebrated modern Kathak dancer, Padma Vibhushan 1986). (2) JAIPUR gharana — emphasis on TECHNICAL footwork (tatkaar), speed, mathematical precision; Rajput warrior origin — exponents Jai Lal, Kundan Lal, Rajendra Gangani. (3) BANARAS gharana — founded by Janaki Prasad; distinctive body movements, less Persian influence, own tatkaar style. Also: Raigarh (smaller). MAIHAR GHARANA is a HINDUSTANI MUSIC gharana (sitar + sarod), founded by BABA ALLAUDDIN KHAN (1862-1972), guru of Ravi Shankar + Ali Akbar Khan — NOT Kathak. TECHNIQUE: chakkars (spins), tatkaar (footwork with ghungroos/ankle-bells), bols (rhythmic syllables), tihais, padhant, abhinaya. COSTUME: Lucknow = Angarkha + churidar/pyjama for men, anarkali/lehenga for women; Jaipur = lehenga-choli-odhani. MUSIC: Hindustani (tabla, sarangi, harmonium). EXPONENTS: Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi (Padma Shri 1975), Kumudini Lakhia, Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Aditi Mangaldas. Maihar is a Hindustani MUSIC gharana of Baba Allauddin Khan, NOT of Kathak.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: KATHAKALI, known for its elaborate MAKEUP + TOWERING HEADGEAR, is the classical dance-drama of:
questions.explanation: KATHAKALI (literally 'story-play') — CLASSICAL DANCE-DRAMA of KERALA, ~17th c. origin; developed by Raja of Kottarakkara (Ramanattam) + Raja of Kottayam (Kottayam Tampuran, author of Nalacharitam + other attakathas). HALLMARKS: (1) ELABORATE MAKEUP + COSTUME — one of the most visually striking dance forms in the world. (2) Traditionally ALL-MALE cast — performances lasted all night in temple courtyards. (3) Based on HINDU epics (Ramayana, Mahabharata) + Puranas. (4) MAKEUP (VESHAM) types colour-coded: (a) PACHA (green face) — noble heroes like Rama, Krishna, Arjuna, Bhima. (b) KATHI (knife) — anti-heroes like Ravana, Duryodhana (green+red). (c) THADI (beard) — Red Beard = villainous (Dushasana); White Beard = Hanuman; Black Beard = hunter/forest-dweller. (d) KARI (black) — demonesses. (e) MINUKKU (shining) — sages, women, Brahmins. (5) CHUTTI — white rice-paste 'beard' extending beyond the chin; (6) towering KIREETAM (headgear) symbolising status. TECHNIQUE: 9 RASAS (emotions), 24 MUDRAS (hand gestures, from Hastalakshana Deepika), elaborate eye exercises (students spend years training). MUSIC: Sopanam (Kerala). Instruments: chenda, maddalam, cymbals. LANGUAGE: Manipravalam (Sanskrit-Malayalam hybrid). Ex: Kalamandalam Gopi, Rama Gopalan, Guru Kunchu Kurup. KERALA KALAMANDALAM — premier institution (founded by Vallathol Narayana Menon, 1930). traditionally performed by male dancers, based on Hindu epics; makeup is colour-coded to character types.

questions.stem: MOHINIYATTAM, the 'dance of the enchantress', comes from which state?
questions.explanation: MOHINIYATTAM ('Mohini' + 'attam' = dance of the enchantress / bewitching woman) — classical dance of KERALA, distinct from Kerala's more dramatic Kathakali. NAME ORIGIN: MOHINI is a female avatar of VISHNU (Churning of the Ocean of Milk — distributed amrita only to devas; Bhasmasura episode — tricked the asura into burning himself). STYLE: CLASSIFIED as LASYA (graceful, feminine) — opposite of Kathakali's TANDAVA (vigorous, masculine). SOLO FEMALE form. COSTUME: distinctive white-cream saree with a GOLDEN BORDER (kasavu saree — Kerala's traditional textile); minimal jewellery; jasmine flowers in hair. MAKEUP: subtle. MUSIC: CARNATIC + Kerala-specific SOPANAM; lyrics in MANIPRAVALAM (Sanskrit-Malayalam hybrid) + Malayalam. DISTINCTIVE FEATURES: SWAYING movements (like the swaying of coconut palms + Kerala's backwaters — oft-cited visual metaphor), circular movements, emphasis on GRACE over ATHLETICS. HISTORY: references in temple records from 16th c.; patronised by KING SWATI THIRUNAL (19th c. Travancore); revived in 20th century by KAVALAM NARAYANA PANICKER + exponent KALAMANDALAM KALYANIKUTTY AMMA ('mother of Mohiniyattam' — revived it from near-extinction after colonial anti-nautch). EXPONENTS: Sunanda Nair, Bharati Shivaji, Kalamandalam Leelamma, Pallavi Krishnan, Smitha Rajan. REPERTOIRE: Cholkettu, Jatiswaram, Varnam, Padam, Tillana (borrowed structure from Bharatanatyam). a LASYA (graceful) classical dance, solo female form, based on the Mohini avatar of Vishnu.

questions.stem: SATTRIYA, added to the list of Classical Dances of India in 2000, originated in:
questions.explanation: SATTRIYA — the classical dance of ASSAM; NEWEST recognised (added by Sangeet Natak Akademi as the 8th classical form in the year 2000). ORIGIN: introduced in the late 15th century by MAHAPURUSHA SRIMANTA SANKARDEVA (1449-1568), the great Vaishnavite saint-reformer of Assam, founder of EKASARANA DHARMA (single-refuge devotion to Vishnu/Krishna). DEVELOPED as a medium of BHAKTI + storytelling in SATRAS (Vaishnava monasteries of Majuli + Barpeta). NAME: from SATRA (monastery). LONG the domain of MONK-DANCERS (Bhakats) — only taken to the public stage in the 20th century, brought out of the satras in the 1950s. TECHNIQUE: combines pure dance (Nritta) + expressive (Nritya); tandava + lasya balance. Hastas + mudras + bhangas as per Natya Shastra + Sankardeva's Hastamuktavali. THEMES: tales of Krishna from Ankiya Naat (plays written by Sankardeva + Madhavadeva). MUSIC: Borgeet (devotional songs composed by Sankardeva + Madhavadeva); instruments = KHOL (drum — signature instrument of Assamese Vaishnavism), CYMBALS (manjira, taal), FLUTE. COSTUME: traditional Assamese silk (muga, pat); paat chador; mekhela sador for women. TYPES: Apsara Nritya, Gopi Nritya, Jhumura, Nadu Bhangi, Bhortal nritya, ankiya naat. EXPONENTS: Jatin Goswami, Ghanakanta Bora, Indira P.P. Bora, Anwesa Mahanta. MAJULI, Assam — the world's largest inhabited river island + centre of Sattras. introduced in the 15th c. by Vaishnavite saint SRIMANTA SANKARDEVA in Satras (monasteries); recognised as 8th classical form by SNA in 2000.

options.option_text: The VILLAGE of KUCHIPUDI (KUCHELAPURAM) in Krishna district, ANDHRA PRADESH, where it was developed by Siddhendra Yogi in the 17th century

questions.explanation: KUCHIPUDI — classical dance of ANDHRA PRADESH, named after the VILLAGE Kuchipudi (originally KUCHELAPURAM) in Krishna district, AP. FOUNDER: SIDDHENDRA YOGI — 17th century Vaishnavite saint-poet, who composed the KUCHIPUDI dance-drama BHAMAKALAPAM (on Satyabhama's jealousy of Rukmini). ORIGINALLY a MALE-only dance-drama tradition (Bhagavatars) performed in temple courtyards. Post-independence, women too learned Kuchipudi + solo formats developed (pioneered by LAKSHMINARAYAN SHASTRI + VEMPATI CHINNA SATYAM — the latter considered the modern father of solo Kuchipudi). UNIQUE FEATURES: (1) TARANGAM — the dancer performs on the RIM of a brass plate with water-pot balanced on the head! (signature item; requires extraordinary skill). (2) JATHISWARAM + shabdam + kalapam. (3) blend of NRITTA + natya, with VACHIKA (speech) playing a role — dancers traditionally spoke dialogues. (4) QUICK-FOOTWORK, sharp BRILLIANT movements, balance. REPERTOIRE: yakshaganams, Krishnaleelas, Bhama Kalapam, Gollakalapam. COSTUME: Silk saree 'typical' south-Indian with fan pleats. MUSIC: Carnatic; instruments = mridangam, flute, violin, tambura. LYRICS: Telugu + Sanskrit. EXPONENTS: Vempati Chinna Satyam, Raja + Radha Reddy, Yamini Krishnamurthy (also Bharatanatyam), Shobha Naidu, Swapna Sundari, Sobha Naidu. DIFF FROM BHARATANATYAM: more ROUNDED + curvilinear; uses more DRAMA; Tarangam unique.

questions.stem: ODISSI, the classical dance of ODISHA, centres around the TRIBHANGA posture. Tribhanga means:
questions.explanation: ODISSI — classical dance of ODISHA, one of the OLDEST classical forms (references + temple sculptures date back to ~2nd c. BCE Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela). TEMPLE-BASED ORIGIN: MAHARIS (temple dancers of the Jagannath Temple at Puri) + later GOTIPUAS (boys dressed as girls, after the Mahari tradition was suppressed). DISTINCTIVE POSTURES: (1) TRIBHANGA — three body bends at NECK-TORSO-KNEE creating an S-shape; (2) CHAUKA — square stance, broad + grounded, associated with Jagannath; (3) ABHANGA — single bend. These are codified in NATYA SHASTRA + ABHINAYA CHANDRIKA. REPERTOIRE: Mangalacharan → Batu (Sthayee) → Pallavi → Tharijham → Abhinaya (Oriya songs of poet Jayadeva's GITA GOVINDA — Ashtapadi) → Moksha. LITERATURE: GITA GOVINDA (12th c. poet JAYADEVA, describes Krishna-Radha love) is central to Odissi abhinaya. MUSIC: Odissi music (distinct from Carnatic + Hindustani); instruments = Pakhawaj/mardala, flute, sitar, violin, manjira. COSTUME: silk saree in traditional patta draping + silver jewellery (tahia = flower crown). REVIVAL: Odissi nearly died out during British era; revived by Kavichandra Kalicharan Pattnaik + Guru DEBA PRASAD DAS + Guru PANKAJ CHARAN DAS + Guru KELUCHARAN MOHAPATRA (greatest modern Odissi guru, Padma Vibhushan 2000; his choreography = Gurukul style). Other exponents: Sanjukta Panigrahi, Sonal Mansingh, Madhavi Mudgal, Aruna Mohanty, Sujata Mohapatra. creating an S-shape characteristic of sculptures in Konark + Bhubaneswar temples; at neck, torso, and knee.

questions.stem: MANIPURI dance is characterised by its GENTLE, FLOWING movements + a distinctive wide-base costume called:
questions.explanation: MANIPURI (JAGOI) — classical dance of MANIPUR, distinctively LYRICAL + GENTLE, with no percussive movements. ORIGIN: ancient tribal dance of the Meitei people; transformed into a devotional form by KING BHAGYACHANDRA (18th c.) after he received a VISION OF KRISHNA + choreographed the RAAS LEELA. THEMES: primarily KRISHNA-RADHA love (Raas Leela — Krishna dances with 16,108 gopis in Vrindavan; Maha Raas, Vasant Raas, Kunj Raas, Nitya Raas are variants). COSTUME: FEMALE dancer wears the iconic POTLOI / KUMIL — a BARREL-shaped stiff skirt reaching the ankles, embellished with mirror work + embroidery; sheer veil over the face. RADHA dances in white veil; KRISHNA in peacock crown, yellow dhoti (male dancer). TECHNIQUE: TANDAVA (masculine) + LASYA (feminine), wafting movements, soft + understated abhinaya (NO exaggerated facial expressions — unlike Kathakali); emphasis on devotion + grace. MUSIC: manipuri ragas; instruments PUNG (drum worn around neck, signature of Manipuri), flute, cymbals, kartal. VAISHNAVISM in Manipur since King Pamheiba's time (~1700s). POLITICAL: Raas Leela performed at the ISKCON world headquarters + across Vaishnava communities globally. RABINDRANATH TAGORE championed Manipuri after seeing it in Sylhet; brought it to Santiniketan (1919). EXPONENTS: Jhaveri Sisters (Ranjana, Nayana, Suverna, Darshana), Guru Bipin Singh + his wife Kalavati Devi, Charu Sija Mathur. SANKIRTANA of Manipur = UNESCO ICH (2013). a barrel-shaped embellished skirt worn by female dancers, depicting Radha + the Gopis in Krishna-bhakti Raaslila.

questions.stem: Match the FOLK DANCE with its STATE: (1) GHOOMAR; (2) LAVANI; (3) BIHU; (4) CHHAU.

options.option_text: Rajasthan; Tamil Nadu; Manipur; Odisha only

questions.explanation: INDIAN FOLK DANCES by STATE (high-yield topic): (1) GHOOMAR — RAJASTHAN; traditionally performed by Rajput women in long ghaghras, pirouetting (ghoom = spin). Rajwada Bhagoria + royal Rajput weddings. Famously highlighted in the 2018 film 'Padmaavat'. (2) LAVANI — MAHARASHTRA; performed to dholki beats; known for powerful rhythm, erotic sringar, women dancers in nauvari saree; popularised in Marathi folk theatre (Tamasha). (3) BIHU — ASSAM; performed during the 3 BIHU FESTIVALS (Rongali / Bohag in April = Assamese New Year, Kongali / Kati in Oct, Bhogali / Magh in Jan). Young men + women in traditional gamosa-mekhela. (4) CHHAU — MASKED MARTIAL DANCE of three states (each with own style): SERAIKELA Chhau (Jharkhand), MAYURBHANJ Chhau (Odisha — no mask), PURULIA Chhau (West Bengal). UNESCO ICH 2010. Uses Ramayana/Mahabharata themes + martial movements. Other famous FOLK DANCES: (5) BHANGRA + GIDDHA (PUNJAB — harvest, Baisakhi); (6) GARBA + DANDIYA RAAS (GUJARAT — Navratri, devotional to Durga); (7) YAKSHAGANA (KARNATAKA — traditional theatre); (8) KALBELIA (RAJASTHAN — snake-charmer tribe, UNESCO ICH 2010); (9) KOLI + LEZIM + TAMASHA (MAHARASHTRA); (10) NATI (HP); (11) JHUMAR (Jharkhand/Haryana); (12) PADAYANI (Kerala); (13) ROUF (Kashmir); (14) CHERAW (bamboo dance — MIZORAM); (15) HOJAGIRI (Tripura); (16) THANG-TA + KHAMBA THOIBI (Manipur); (17) SINGHI CHHAM (Sikkim); (18) LAMBADI (Telangana).
